ADS — Ads Agent says OPTIMIZE, do not launch new ads yet. Reason: only ~16 days of data and attribution live since 7/22, so there is no clean cost-per-lead to justify splitting the $30/day cap. Contract Manufacturing is the high-intent campaign but budget-starved (32% of impressions lost to budget). White Label Samples is weaker and mixed-intent.
Proposed plan, inside the existing cap (no spend increase): Samples $10 -> $5/day, Contract Manufacturing $20 -> $25/day; add sitelinks/callouts/structured snippets to lift ad strength and regain rank-lost impressions; mine search terms for negatives. Revisit new ads after ~2 weeks of attributed data.
Oversight: recommendation is consistent with the standing rule to fix attribution before adding spend, and it stays read-only until you approve. Verified separately: the Ads Agent callback channel published for the first time on this request — the v12 silence is resolved.

5 STANDARD MOLDS, 3 oz / 3.5 oz — these are the standard stock formats to offer (no custom tooling, no new mold cost):
1. Cylinder bottle, HDPE, 100 ml / 3.4 oz — disc top or flip top. The default lotion/serum body.
2. Boston round, PET, 100 ml / 3.4 oz — treatment pump or dropper. Reads premium for serums/oils.
3. Airless pump bottle, 100 ml / 3.4 oz — for actives and anhydrous formulas that need no-air dispensing.
4. Squeeze tube, LDPE, 100 ml / 3.4 oz — flip top or nozzle. Cheapest per unit, best for creams/gels/masks.
5. Straight-sided jar, PP or glass, 100 ml / 3.4 oz — screw cap with liner. For balms, butters, thick creams.
Note: 3 oz and 3.5 oz both land on the same 100 ml stock body — 3 oz is an underfill of it, not a separate mold. Confirm before quoting: exact fill (3.0 vs 3.4 oz), closure choice per format, and decoration method (label vs silkscreen). If you want these five locked as PLL's published standard 3 oz lineup with per-unit pricing, say so and I will build the one-page customer sheet.

APPROVAL NEEDED: reallocate the daily cap Samples $5 / Contract Manufacturing $25 and add the ad assets? Yes or no.
spoken_text: Two answers. On ads: optimize, don't launch new ones. There isn't enough attributed data yet to justify splitting the budget, and Contract Manufacturing is losing about a third of its impressions to budget while Samples underperforms. The fix stays inside your current cap. On packaging: three ounce and three and a half ounce both use the same hundred milliliter stock body, and the five standard molds are the cylinder bottle, the Boston round, the airless pump, the squeeze tube, and the straight-sided jar. Details are on screen. One approval: shift the cap to five dollars Samples and twenty-five dollars Contract Manufacturing, and add the ad assets. Yes or no?
